title: oscal-validate package report
description: The shape of `oscal-validate package <directory> --format json`. A package report exists only when every file in the directory was read: a directory holding a file that cannot be read exits 2 and writes no report, so `documents` is never empty. Every report carries `package_report_schema_version`, the version of this document, which moves independently of the per-document report schema that each embedded `report` conforms to. `additionalProperties` is false everywhere on purpose: a consumer that validates against this schema learns about a new key rather than ignoring it.

package_report_schema_version.description: The version of this schema the report conforms to.

root.description: The directory as it was given on the command line.

documents.description: How many members were read and validated. Equal to the length of `documents`.
One entry per member, in path order.

import_graph.description: Every import each member writes itself, not the ones reached through it. An observation; it gates nothing.

imports_not_in_package.description: The imports in `import_graph` whose name no member answers to, not even by file name without extension.

unreferenced.description: Members no other member imports. A package's top-level document is always among them; this is a map of the set's roots, not a list of defects.

uuid_collisions.description: UUIDs declared in more than one member, with every declaration. Package policy, not a finding, and never gating.

summary.description: Severity totals across every member's findings, plus the size of each cross-document section. Only the severities decide the exit code, and only as the per-document command does.

notes.description: Fixed sentences stating what the cross-document sections do not mean.

exit_code.description: The exit code `oscal-validate <path> --resolve <root>` returns for this member. Never 2: a member that could not be read means no report was written.

report.description: The complete per-document report for this member, conforming to report.schema.json at the report_schema_version it carries. It is byte for byte the report `oscal-validate <path> --resolve <root> --format json` writes, parsed.

from.description: The member the import is written in.

target_name.description: The file name the href names, or null for a fragment this tool could not turn into one.

resolved_to.description: The member the import resolved to, or null when none answered.

matched_by.description: How the name was matched, or null when the import did not resolve.

candidates.description: Every member whose name matched: empty when none did, and never more than one, because within one directory no two .json files share a file name or a file name without extension, which are the only two keys import matching uses.
